rationale: This is a mechanical union of two archived signals — the gen-8 "Broad-Scope Externally Funded Expansion" (legs 1–2 verbatim) plus the gen-0 "Deployed External Capital Bottleneck" cash-deployment leg (leg 3 verbatim) — so it is a recombination rather than a new mechanism, and both parents already sit squarely on the known asset-growth / net-external-financing anomaly.

The first two legs replicate the archive's strongest signal, but substituting the debt-retirement burden for the cash-deployment leg is a genuinely different economic condition (refinancing pressure rather than capital deployment), the sign is internally consistent, and it is testable — though the risk is that a weakly informative maturity leg simply dilutes an already-strong parent.

This is essentially "Simultaneous Capex-Leverage Peaks" (gen 8) stapled to the financing legs of "Maturity-Downgrade Investment" (gen 7) with a SUMRANK softening, which the reasoning itself concedes, making it a cosmetic recombination whose parents each delivered only marginal alpha.

It merges two archived positive-sign signals ("Balance-Sheet-Slack Debt Investment" and "Termed-Out Investment Financing"), but the soft SUMRANK of unused debt capacity and maturity improvement is a coherent joint "financing quality" construct with a consistent expected sign and two independently supportive parents, so it is worth one test even though it is close to a merge.

This is the gen-2 "Post-Investment Financing Shortfall" with the hard cash-depletion leg softened by averaging in a leverage TS_RANK — a cosmetic variant that is unlikely to repair the parent's weak Fama-MacBeth slope, since softening a leg typically blurs rather than sharpens cross-sectional identification.

It fuses two archived signals whose FMB slopes and FF5 alphas already pointed in opposite directions (gen-7 and gen-8 both had positive t-stats with negative alphas), and the third leg subtracts a share-count growth rate from a change in an equity ratio — badly mismatched scales, so the rank is effectively driven by dilution alone rather than the stated joint condition.
